chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the heart jingles in the chest, seeking the truth; so when it finds it, it becomes calm and settles.
Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) recited this verse:
So whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands his chest for Islam; and whoever He intends to misguide, He makes his chest narrow and constricted, as though he were ascending to the sky.
Up to His Words: 'as though he were ascending to the sky'.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the heart's 'jingle' and 'expansion' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the psychological and spiritual dynamics of the heart (qalb), describing its agitation (tajaljul) as a natural search for divine truth that culminates in tranquility (itmi'nan) upon recognition. This narrative underscores the Shia concept of the heart's innate disposition (fitrah) and the transformative effect of divine guidance, linking internal spiritual states to the external manifestation of faith. The reference to Quran 6:125 serves to contrast the expansive peace of the guided with the constriction of the misguided, highlighting the metaphysical reality of spiritual ascent and descent.
